title: Monde Selection: Why Are Gold Medals Everywhere?｜Curio Archive
description:
Walk into any East Asian convenience store and Belgian gold medals are everywhere—so why does Belgium itself have zero entries on the official 2026 Nominee Label list?
For anyone who has ever been drawn to that shiny gold award sticker at a convenience store or drugstore and wondered what it is really worth.

Drawing on Monde Selection's official FAQ and evaluation methodology, authorized Japanese agent Foods R&D's official euro fee schedule and 2018 global and Japan statistics, the October 2024 press release announcing the 2025 abolition of Silver and Bronze awards, Monde Selection's official 416-product Nominee Label 2026 list, a Meijo University Meijo Review marketing study on Japan's 2005 premium beer boom, and a Diamond Online column by a Tokyo Stock Exchange Prime-listed e-commerce executive, this video unpacks in chronological order the 1961 non-competitive absolute scoring model, per-product fees over €1,000 and the three-year licensing clock, the 2005 Japanese beer 23x sales spark, the 2018 scorecard and nearly 60% repeat-entry rate, the 2025 decision to retire Silver and Bronze, East Asia's shelf prisoner's dilemma, and a 3-second guide to reading the seal.

This channel has no affiliation with any brand mentioned. Illustrations in this episode are AI-generated.
Data as of 2026-11-23

m001.text: Walk into a Taiwan store—gold seals pack the shelf.

m002.text: Snacks, fish oil, noodles—all stamped Monde Selection.

m003.text: You'd think it's a food Olympics with one champ.

m004.text: Yet five rivals on one shelf all won gold. How?

m006.text: Stranger still, Europe barely knows this Belgian award.

m007.text: Japan alone took over 1,300 awards—half the world!

m008.text: How did a niche European seal rule Asian shelves?

m009.text: Our archive pulled up the rules and fee sheets.

m010.text: Today, let's see how it got Asia lining up to pay.

m011.text: The story starts back in Brussels, in 1961.

m012.text: Back then, European food contests were subjective.

m013.text: Monde Selection launched—now run by a private firm.

m014.text: It's no scam: real experts blind-test every item.

m015.text: If judging is real, why do rivals all win at once?

m016.text: Their site states the rule: it's not a contest!

m017.text: Items never compete—it's like hotel star ratings.

m018.text: Out of 100: 60 Bronze, 70 Silver, 80 Gold, 90 Grand Gold!

m019.text: One block fits ten five-star hotels—same for snacks.

m020.text: Pass the bar, get a medal—no wonder over 91% win!

m021.text: Sounds generous, right? Yet this is no charity.

m022.text: No cap, expert judges—how do they make money?

m023.text: The fee sheet explains: they charge per item, not brand!

m024.text: Same snack, new flavor? Pay a brand-new fee!

m027.text: Brands pay customs and air freight to Europe.

m028.text: To grab global orders, even chilled foods get a fix!

m029.text: Japanese chilled goods pay extra for local judging!

m030.text: Worse yet: once you win, can you print it forever?

m031.text: No! The medal license lasts just three years.

m032.text: Skip renewal and every gold badge must come off.

m033.text: A 3-year subscription loop running six decades!

m034.text: If Europe barely cares, who sparked Asia's craze?

m035.text: The spark was 2005: Suntory's Premium Malt's beer.

m036.text: Suntory's beer unit had lost money since the 1960s.

m037.text: A Meijo University paper notes 500,000 cases in 2004.

m038.text: Morale was low, so in 2005 they sent it to Belgium!

m039.text: Big news hit Tokyo: Japan's first beer Grand Gold!

m040.text: They ran big ads: Grand Gold for weekend treats.

m041.text: Ads aired—and Grand Gold sparked a buying frenzy!

m042.text: Orders surged so fast factories had to pause sales!

m043.text: Suntory pushed gift sets—then made a bolder move.

m044.text: Skipping the 3-year rest, it chased a 3-year streak!

m045.text: Despite yearly crop shifts, it won three straight!

m046.text: With that three-peat badge, how high did sales jump?

m048.text: Nearly 23 times its 2004 volume in four years!

m049.text: It led premium beer and turned the unit profitable!

m050.text: That miracle shook Asia—brands rushed to apply!

m051.text: As stickers filled shelves, shoppers grew skeptical:

m052.text: If everyone wins, is it really just pay-to-win?

m053.text: Back to 2018 data: over 200 entries still failed.

m054.text: Losers stay quiet—shelves only show survivors!

m055.text: Yet high win rates don't mean judges go easy.

m056.text: The test room is full of seasoned repeat players!

m057.text: Look at Japan's over 1,300 winners—it's crystal clear.

m059.text: In food, just 4.9% of rookies won Grand Gold!

m060.text: For repeat winners in that class, it hit 27%!

m061.text: With regulars driving income, how do they keep them?

m062.text: In 2018, they rolled out detailed scoring reports!

m063.text: Brands tweak recipes from reports and come right back!

m064.text: Once scoring is cracked, the gold list grows longer!

m065.text: Yet flooding shelves with medals diluted the brand!

m066.text: Even headquarters felt trust in old tiers fading.

m067.text: On October 3, 2024, they linked with Tokyo press.

m068.text: They admitted the 60-year system caused confusion.

m069.text: Nobel Prize comparisons drew years of backlash.

m070.text: Gold, Silver, Bronze made shoppers think it's a race!

m071.text: To split top scores from basics, they overhauled it!

m072.text: First shift in 64 years: Silver and Bronze end in 2025!

m073.text: Only Gold tiers stay; 70 to 79 gets Nominee Label.

m074.text: So what happens to old Silver and Bronze medals?

m075.text: They expire after three years, with no renewal.

m076.text: Won't cutting two tiers hurt their fee income?

m077.text: No! They sell scarce prestige, not stickers.

m078.text: Cutting lower tiers guards prestige and pushes past 80!

m079.text: Prestige rises while the fee engine stays intact!

m080.text: Even after reform, why do brands still apply?

m081.text: In November, Diamond Online ran a candid column.

m082.text: A Tokyo-listed e-commerce CEO shared a meeting.

m083.text: Staff asked: Monde Selection is everywhere—why pay?

m084.text: Then the CEO's question silenced the whole room.

m085.text: "If we skip it, what if rivals add the seal first?"

m086.text: Panic hit—nobody wanted to lag, so they applied!

m087.text: See it now? Classic shelf prisoner's dilemma!

m088.text: Shoppers decide in 3 seconds—nobody reads lab specs.

m089.text: Online you can't taste it—the seal buys fast trust.

m090.text: Big brands aren't chasing first—it's pure insurance!

m091.text: One adds it, rivals follow—a shelf arms race.

m092.text: How fierce is Asia's race? Check the 2026 list!

m093.text: On the 2026 Nominee Label list, what's Asia's share?

m094.text: Out of 416 items, Asia took a massive 363!

m095.text: Taiwan led with 126, Japan 83, mainland China 61.

m096.text: Hong Kong 27, Korea 15—all Europe had just 11!

m097.text: America had 2, Belgium zero—the West stayed quiet.

m098.text: You know the game—how do you read it in 3 seconds?

m099.text: Pick up the pack and check which tier is printed.

m100.text: Grand Gold, Gold, and Nominee set different bars.

m101.text: Next, glance at the year to see if it's recent.

m102.text: Recent years show a brand still pays for audits.

m103.text: See it as passing a quality bar, not magic hype.

m104.text: It proves solid quality, not the single best choice.

m105.text: Best tip: flip the pack for ingredients and reviews!

m106.text: Tasty or worth the markup? You're the real judge!

m107.text: This 60-year Belgian model sells 3 seconds of peace.

m108.text: Peel that filter—looks like a shelf war, right?

m109.text: That's the business truth behind Monde Selection.
